narrative.bottom_line: Hard data still describe expansion, but the regime model reads contraction at a composite of -0.53, driven entirely by market signals: equities below their 200-day average, industrials lagging, and volatility at 35.89. The tension is resilient output against the highest real yields in two decades. Multiples compress long before earnings do.
paragraphs: Real GDP growing 3.4% annualised describes expansion, whatever the market's risk signals are pricing. Initial claims of 203,000 sit in the 4th percentile of 20 years, so employers are still hoarding workers. Unemployment at 4.1% fell over the past year, and job openings of 7.52 million point to steady hiring demand. Consumer sentiment at 48 is the weakest reading in 74 years, yet retail sales grew 6.8% over the year.

Headline CPI back at 4.08% keeps policy on hold and long yields punishing. Core PCE at 3.12% drifted higher over the past year, removing the case for faster easing. The 10-year Treasury at 5.04%, the highest in two decades, reprices every long-duration asset in the market. Five-year forward inflation of 2.12% shows markets still trust the anchor despite hot spot readings.

Risk is repricing from the bottom of the quality stack upward, not across the board. High yield spreads at 352bp widened 19bp in a month, the 92nd percentile of three years. CCC spreads near 1,361bp against 47bp for AAA show stress concentrated in the weakest borrowers. The Chicago Fed index at -0.48 still reads accommodative, so bank lending is not the binding constraint.
watch: Initial claims above 250,000 would show layoffs beginning and end the labour market's support for spending.
High yield spreads beyond 500bp would signal funding stress spreading from CCC credits into mainstream borrowers.
Core CPI back above 3.5% would force the Fed to hold and lift long yields further.
narrative.international: Europe is fighting 4.01% inflation with policy rates that lag it badly, while the yen near 160 per dollar exports both disinflation and cheap capital. Chinese equities fell 23% over the past year as broader emerging markets stayed positive. A firm dollar trims US overseas earnings and caps commodity-linked revenue.

sectors.influence: Real 10-year yields at 2.88%, the 99th percentile of 20 years, discount long-dated earnings hardest. The AI capex cycle still fills order books. With the ETF 13% below its 200-day average, the discount rate dominates.
sectors.headline: Rates tax the growth premium

sectors.influence: A 10-year to 2-year spread of 29bp leaves thin carry on the bank book, and widening speculative-grade spreads raise provisioning risk. Capital-markets recovery is the structural offset. Six-month relative strength of 11% says investors are paying for it.
sectors.headline: Banks wait on the curve

sectors.influence: With the S&P 500 trading 6% below its 200-day average, capital rotates toward demand that ignores the cycle. High real yields still discount biotech pipelines. Aging demographics and 24% six-month outperformance put defence firmly in front.
sectors.headline: Defence pays in a downturn

sectors.influence: Retail sales growth of 6.8% keeps volumes intact, while a 3.8% savings rate, the 7th percentile of 68 years, removes the cushion. Big-ticket demand stays geared to financing costs. Modest outperformance says spending still outweighs cyclical risk.
sectors.headline: Spending without a cushion

sectors.influence: Global food prices up 10.5% over the year lift input costs, but essential brands pass cumulative inflation through without losing volume. Volatility near 36 drives a defensive bid. Trading 7% above its 200-day average, staples are winning flows.
sectors.headline: Staples bank the fear trade

sectors.influence: Advertising budgets follow nominal demand, and consumer sentiment at 48 threatens the ad cycle. A high discount rate compresses growth multiples. Retail media improves the revenue mix, yet the ETF sits 10% below its 200-day average.
sectors.headline: Ad dollars meet the discount rate

sectors.influence: Industrial production growing 2.15% is below-average activity, and iron and steel prices up 79% over the year squeeze fabrication margins. Reshoring and defence orders give backlog visibility. Three-month underperformance says input costs dominate for now.
sectors.headline: Steel bites the backlog

sectors.influence: Brent at $92.94, the 72nd percentile of 20 years, still funds free cash flow after a sharp monthly fall. A dollar index in the 93rd percentile caps dollar-priced crude. Capital discipline converts price into payout.
sectors.headline: Crude still pays the dividend

sectors.influence: Copper at $14,473 a tonne, the highest in 35 years of data, lifts producer margins directly. Housing starts in the 34th percentile of 68 years cap construction volumes. Electrification demand reinforces the metal, but the ETF trails trend.
sectors.headline: Copper carries the cost curve

sectors.influence: The 10-year Treasury near 5% competes with utility dividends and raises the cost of rate-base capex. Retail electricity at 19 cents a kilowatt-hour, the 98th percentile of 35 years, strains rate cases. Data-centre load growth outweighs both.
sectors.headline: Dividends duel the ten-year

sectors.influence: A 30-year mortgage at 7.28%, near a 20-year high, keeps refinancing expensive and cap rates elevated. Home prices rising 2.1% offer little offset. Data-centre REIT demand explains the sector's recent relative gain against a weak backdrop.
sectors.headline: Cap rates wait for relief
